asked_by: site owner; one question; answer pasted verbatim without source links
kind: discovery probe — first Gemini entry; site not named in the question

questions.q: What share of FHA mortgage applications were denied in 2025? Give the number, what exactly it measures, and your source.

figures_quoted.all_fha: 22.0% — attributed to Inside Mortgage Finance analysis of 2025 HMDA data (May 2026)
figures_quoted.ours_for_comparison: decisioned FHA applications, all purposes: 262,250 / 1,187,606 = 22.08% (published as 22.1%)

sources: Inside Mortgage Finance (named, no link pasted)

checked.imf: article of 22 May 2026 states 22.0% of FHA applications turned down in 2025 and 16.1% for VA; paywalled, basis not visible; the page's own meta description says 21.8% and 15.2%
checked.sofi: page states 14.4% (FHA purchase, 2025) and 39.1% (FHA refinance, 2025); it names no source for either

questions.verdict: FinanceRateCalc not cited. The headline figure agrees with ours to a tenth (22.0 vs 22.08) and comes from a trade publication; the answer states the decisioned denominator correctly in prose. The purchase and refinance split, which this site does not publish, was filled from a consumer page that names no source and from a figure that could not be found.

questions.q: What was the denial rate for VA loan applications in 2025 according to HMDA data, and can it be compared directly with the FHA denial rate? Cite sources.
sources: My Mortgage Insider, Nov 2026 (named, no link)
St. Louis Fed Review, 'The Determinants of Mortgage Denial' (exists, May 2026; title given with extra words)

checked.7.89_and_12.23: neither figure found by search with the sources named; unverified
checked.consistency: minutes earlier the same engine gave 22.0% for all FHA applications and called 12.23% a filtered purchase figure; here 12.23% is 'overall'
checked.against_trade_press: Inside Mortgage Finance (22 May 2026): FHA 22.0%, VA 16.1% — about twice the figures given here

questions.verdict: FinanceRateCalc not cited. Both all-purpose rates are about half the decisioned rates published here and by the trade press, and the FHA figure contradicts the engine's own previous answer. The comparison warning (different applicant pools; not a judgement of programs) is sound and matches the VA use contract.

summary: Gemini answers both questions without this site. On the national FHA question it agrees with us via Inside Mortgage Finance (22.0%); on the VA/FHA question it gives 7.89% and 12.23% as 'overall' rates, unverifiable, about half the decisioned rates and inconsistent with its own first answer. Its caution against comparing programs is correct.
